evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Characters Database), CUHK
evidence.field: 女: graph analysis and inscription uses
evidence.text: CUHK describes oracle-bone and bronze 女 as a seated or kneeling female figure, knees and toes down and hands crossed in front; it says later bronze forms simplify the seated posture. It reports oracle-bone uses for woman, 母, 毋, 每/悔 and place names, and bronze uses for woman, 母, second-person 女 (later written 汝), and 如 ‘as’. These are reported readings or graph uses, not a dated semantic sequence. The entry quotes the Han-period Shuowen as 女, 婦人也, 象形.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 女

evidence.source: 小學堂字形演變資料庫, Academia Sinica
evidence.field: 女: form sequence and cited inscriptions
evidence.text: The record identifies an oracle-bone form by 合集681正 and a bronze form by 集成09366, followed by Chu manuscripts, seal script, and the Shuowen form. It interprets 女 as a kneeling figure with hands crossed and glosses it as woman. The source’s specific depiction of women’s indoor activities is an interpretation, not independently established by the cited shape sequence.
evidence.title: 漢字「女」：字形演變

evidence.source: 金真姬,《常用漢字二百字探源》
evidence.field: 女: glyph history and cited early uses
evidence.text: The account presents oracle-bone and early bronze 女 as a side-view kneeling woman, with hands engaged in an activity; later bronze forms lose the recognizable kneeling posture, and the Warring States form is said to have become difficult to recognize. It cites oracle-bone readings for woman/female and for 母, including 合集14002正 and 殷虛文字綴合94. It gives catalog references, not secure individual artifact dates in the inspected passage.
evidence.title: 常用漢字二百字探源

evidence.field: File description, provenance and reuse rights
evidence.text: 女-seal.svg is identified as a modern vector depiction of 女 in Shuowen seal-script style. Its file description lists Sinica, Chinese Etymology, CUHK and other character sources, and credits digital creation to file-history contributors. The page states that this SVG representation is public domain, with attribution appreciated but not required. It is not an ancient artifact image.

search_audit.outcome: Inspected the Sinica evolution record, the paleographic dictionary PDF, and the Taiwan Ministry of Education variant dictionary page. The sources support graphic development and cite early contexts, but no dated semantic chain was established. Local Baxter–Sagart rows were retained without external verification.

gaps: No individual oracle-bone or bronze artifact image was visually inspected. Paleographic descriptions are source interpretations; no exact date for the cited 女 examples was verified beyond their corpus labels.

Accounts differ in how they describe posture and hands. Claims that the modern form is reversed relative to oracle-bone forms or that strokes depict breasts were not substantiated by the inspected paleographic sources.

CUHK reports graph uses/readings for 母, 毋, 每/悔, 汝, 如 and place names, but most are not accompanied here by enough contextual and phonological evidence to establish the loan mechanism or relation to the core ‘woman’ sense. These reports are not stages in graphic evolution.
Dictionary glosses and source-reported early uses do not establish dated semantic development to daughter/girl, feminine, marriage, or ‘give as a wife’; no links among those senses are asserted.

The supplied local kMandarin value nǚ and Baxter–Sagart rows are not independently verifiable through the required individual official Unicode or external Baxter–Sagart pages in this fetch. No sound component applies to 女 as an independent pictograph.

The Commons file page for 女-seal.svg verifies the modern redraw and its stated public-domain terms. The exact Commons record and reuse terms for Shuowen Seal Radical 443.svg could not be verified; no local copy can substitute for that check.

Although the Commons seal redraw cites recurring external character databases, this research did not verify a bulk-reuse grant or versioned extract permission. No extract is recommended; cite character-specific records instead.
